title: Finding
description: One vulnerability finding. Written append-only as workspace/findings/<id>.json. The `status` flag + `history` are what drive the streaming convergence and the reproduction feedback loop.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. sha1(track + vuln_class + sink.file + sink.line). Same logical bug must hash to the same id so re-runs do not duplicate.

correlation_id.description: Groups findings that share a root cause (e.g. one tainted source reaching many sinks). Used by convergence for de-dup.

vuln_class.description: e.g. sql-injection, command-injection, xss, deserialization, idor, broken-access-control, auth-bypass, business-logic.

cwe.description: e.g. CWE-89. Pulled from Semgrep rule metadata when available.

severity_estimate.description: Producer's first guess. Triage may revise after reproduction.

description.description: What makes this attacker-controlled (e.g. GET param).

flow.description: Ordered source->sink path. Each hop is a step the taint/reasoning crossed.

sanitizers_seen.description: Validation/escaping encountered on the path. Empty = no sanitization.

evidence.description: LLM reasoning for why this is (or isn't) exploitable.

status.description: Lifecycle. candidate -> cross_validated -> reproduced -> confirmed. Repro failure can route to false_positive OR needs_reanalysis (feedback loop).

env.description: Which warm target env was used.

history.description: Audit trail. Every stage that touches this finding appends an entry. Makes the feedback loop debuggable.
